function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

message.content:
**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| Aspect | What Turbonomic Brings | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|--------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Visibility** | Aggregates real‑time telemetry from all workloads—VMs, containers, serverless functions, databases, etc.—across on‑prem, GCP, AWS, Azure, and other clouds into a single pane. | Unilever can see the entire application stack without switching dashboards or pulling logs from disparate sources. |
| **Intelligent Workload Placement** | Uses machine‑learning models to predict performance, cost, and compliance outcomes for each workload under different placement scenarios. | Enables Unilever to automatically move workloads to the most cost‑efficient or performance‑optimal environment while staying compliant with internal policies. |
| **Proactive Capacity Planning** | Continuously forecasts resource demand (CPU, memory, I/O) and recommends right‑size actions before bottlenecks occur. | Prevents over‑provisioning (cost savings) and under‑provisioning (performance degradation). |
| **Policy‑Based Automation** | Lets Unilever define high‑level business rules (e.g., “Keep latency < 200 ms for e‑commerce”) and automatically enforces them across all clouds. | Reduces manual toil and ensures consistent service levels across regions and providers. |
| **Cost Optimization & Chargeback** | Tracks actual usage vs. committed capacity, attributes spend to business units, and suggests savings opportunities. | Gives Unilever clear visibility into where money is being spent and how to reduce waste. |
| **Security & Compliance** | Detects misconfigurations, unauthorized changes, and policy violations in real time. | Helps Unilever meet regulatory requirements (GDPR, PCI‑DSS, etc.) across multiple jurisdictions. |
| **Observability Integration** | Integrates with existing monitoring/telemetry stacks (Prometheus, Datadog, New Relic, etc.) and feeds insights back into those systems. | Allows Unilever to keep its preferred observability tools while benefiting from Turbonomic’s AI layer. |

**Key Differences Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Provider Tools**

| Feature | Turbonomic | GCP Native (e.g., Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Profiler) | AWS Native (e.g., CloudWatch, Trusted Advisor) | Azure Native (e.g., Monitor, Advisor) |
|---------|------------|----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud, cross‑infrastructure (on‑prem + all major clouds) | Single‑cloud, provider‑specific | Single‑cloud, provider‑specific | Single‑cloud, provider‑specific |
| **AI/ML Engine** | Proprietary ML models that learn from historical data and simulate future states | Basic anomaly detection, limited predictive analytics | Basic anomaly detection, limited predictive analytics | Basic anomaly detection, limited predictive analytics |
| **Workload Placement** | Automated recommendations and auto‑execution across clouds | No automated placement; manual scaling only | No automated placement; manual scaling only | No automated placement; manual scaling only |
| **Cost Modeling** | Real‑time cost attribution, chargeback, and savings simulation | Cost Explorer provides reports but no proactive recommendations | Cost Explorer provides reports but no proactive recommendations | Cost Management provides reports but no proactive recommendations |
| **Policy Enforcement** | Declarative business policies that drive automation | Limited policy engine (e.g., IAM roles, budgets) | Limited policy engine (e.g., Service Control Policies) | Limited policy engine (e.g., Policy Insights) |
| **Integration Layer** | Unified API and UI that aggregates metrics from all clouds | Native dashboards per provider | Native dashboards per provider | Native dashboards per provider |
| **Automation** | Auto‑scale, auto‑move, auto‑right‑size, auto‑chargeback | Manual scaling, manual budget alerts | Manual scaling, manual budget alerts | Manual scaling, manual budget alerts |
| **Observability Depth** | Deep telemetry ingestion (metrics, logs, traces) + AI insights | Provider‑native telemetry | Provider‑native telemetry | Provider‑native telemetry |

### Bottom Line

Turbonomic acts as a *single, AI‑driven control plane* that sits above the native observability and management tools of GCP, AWS, and Azure. While each cloud offers powerful monitoring and cost‑management features, they are siloed and require separate expertise. Turbonomic unifies these capabilities, adds predictive intelligence, and automates optimization decisions across the entire multi‑cloud environment—exactly what Unilever needs to run its global supply chain, retail, and consumer‑goods workloads efficiently and cost‑effectively.
